rubric.claim_score: 0 unsupported/contradicted; 1 partly supported or named comparator missing; 2 directly supported in paper/document context
rubric.decision_score: 0 baseline or matched test absent; 1 both present but numerical acceptance threshold unset; 2 baseline, matched test and threshold specified

cases.question: More supervised examples or another small GRPO run?

claim_scores.claim: The SRL authors caution that SFT on modest sets of long demonstrations may overfit and report that both SFT and outcome-based RL struggle on challenging tasks.
claim_scores.reason: SRL introduction §1 discusses modest-scale long demonstrations, overfitting, and failure of SFT/outcome RL on difficult reasoning.

claim_scores.claim: Med-RLVR uses an outcome correctness and format verifier for its medical multiple-choice reward.
claim_scores.reason: Med-RLVR §2 specifies format check and gold option-letter correctness reward.

A.decision_reason: Existing v5/trajectory baseline and a matched review/later comparison are named, but numerical training and reward-agreement gates are explicitly unset.
A.comments: Appropriately defers training. SRL/Med-RLVR concern different tasks and rewards, so they do not establish corrected SFT superiority here.

claim_scores.claim: DeepSeekMath GRPO replaces PPO’s learned value-model baseline with scores from multiple outputs to the same question.
claim_scores.reason: DeepSeekMath §4.1.1 defines group-score baseline in place of PPO critic.

claim_scores.claim: DeepSeekMath’s reported RL phase used about 144,000 math questions and sampled 64 outputs per question.
claim_scores.reason: DeepSeekMath §4.2 gives about 144K RL questions and 64 sampled outputs per question.

claim_scores.claim: ReTool trained a code-integrated cold-start SFT model before applying RL with interleaved code execution.
claim_scores.reason: ReTool §2 gives cold-start code-integrated SFT followed by interleaved code-execution RL.

claim_scores.claim: ReTool used a rule-based final-answer correctness reward against ground truth and did not include code executability in that reward.
claim_scores.reason: ReTool §2.3.1 defines rule-based final-answer accuracy reward and explicitly excludes code-executability reward.

claim_scores.claim: DeepSeek-R1’s authors say reward reliability is central to RL and that reliable signals are hard to construct for open-ended tasks.
claim_scores.reason: DeepSeek-R1 §6 and §G.1 discuss reward reliability and difficulty for open-ended tasks.

claim_scores.claim: DeepSeek-R1’s authors report reward hacking with a helpfulness reward: reward rose while Codeforces performance fell.
claim_scores.reason: DeepSeek-R1 §B.5 and Figure 6 show helpfulness reward rising while Codeforces performance falls.

B.decision_reason: Fixed v5/few-shot comparator, paired 40-question review, and explicit support, error, latency, and cost thresholds are given; later GRPO gate remains unset.
B.comments: Appropriately treats the +3/20 gate as a development pilot and requires a separate held-out test; no causal SFT-versus-GRPO result is claimed.

cases.question: BM25 alone or hybrid retrieval plus reranking for long research papers?

claim_scores.claim: SciRet reports hybrid BM25 plus dense recall gains in its scientific corpus, while an MS MARCO cross-encoder reduced precision in its tested setup.
claim_scores.reason: SciRet abstract supports hybrid recall/robustness relative to sparse and dense systems and lower reranker precision; the claim omits the sparse/dense comparator and pseudo-label qualification.

claim_scores.claim: Lit3R combines sparse and dense retrieval with reranking for literature-grounded QA.
claim_scores.reason: Lit3R abstract describes BM25 sparse+dense retrieval and cross-encoder reranking for literature QA.

A.decision_reason: BM25 baseline, paired three-way retrieval test, and numerical evidence-hit/answer thresholds are specified; latency ceiling remains unset.
A.comments: SciRet pseudo-labels favor its hybrid retrieval; a QASPER evidence and answer review is needed. D3/other sources do not license a production switch.

claim_scores.claim: QASPER pairs full research papers with human-selected supporting evidence, allowing evidence retrieval to be evaluated separately from answer generation.
claim_scores.reason: QASPER abstract states full-paper questions with human answer evidence.

claim_scores.claim: SciRet found hybrid retrieval more robust than sparse or dense alone in its scientific corpus, but its pseudo-relevance labels were derived from the hybrid system.
claim_scores.reason: SciRet abstract explicitly compares sparse, dense, hybrid and discloses hybrid-derived pseudo-relevance labels.

claim_scores.claim: SciRet reported that an MS MARCO-trained cross-encoder reduced precision on its scientific corpus.
claim_scores.reason: SciRet abstract explicitly reports lower precision with MS MARCO cross-encoder.

claim_scores.claim: A QASPER study examined a retriever-ranker-reader pipeline and reported that stage choices affected answer quality.
claim_scores.reason: ACL Anthology abstract states retriever-ranker-reader experiments on QASPER and effects of stage modeling choices on answer prediction.

B.decision_reason: BM25 comparator, fixed-budget ablations, and evidence-hit plus p95 thresholds are specified.
B.comments: Acknowledges SciRet label bias and measures this corpus. Complete human-evidence-set hit is stronger than a single-span proxy.

cases.question: Prefix caching or speculative decoding for two concurrent Qwen3-8B readers?

claim_scores.claim: vLLM prefix caching reuses KV cache for matching prefixes and reduces prefill work, but it does not reduce decoding time.
claim_scores.reason: vLLM APC introduction and Limits say matched-prefix KV reuse skips prefill and does not reduce decode time.

claim_scores.claim: vLLM documents speculative decoding primarily as a way to reduce inter-token latency for medium-to-low-QPS, memory-bound workloads.
claim_scores.reason: vLLM Speculative Decoding guide introduction names inter-token latency and medium-to-low-QPS memory-bound workload.

claim_scores.claim: A serving study found speculative-decoding speedups often shrink as server load rises and depend on draft acceptance and model sizes.
claim_scores.reason: Latency-model abstract reports load-sensitive speedups and dependence on acceptance and model sizes.

A.decision_reason: Cache-off baseline, same two-client replay, and TTFT/end-to-end/prefix-reuse thresholds are specified.
A.comments: vLLM documentation supports the mechanism, not a speedup for this exact two-reader workload. Prefix identity, cache hits, and decode fraction must be measured.

claim_scores.claim: KVFlow reports that its prefix-cache gains shrink as outputs grow because decoding dominates runtime.
claim_scores.reason: KVFlow §4.1 results explicitly state relative gain declines as output tokens grow because decode dominates.

claim_scores.claim: Speculative decoding targets serial autoregressive decode steps by drafting and verifying multiple tokens in parallel.
claim_scores.reason: Speculative Decoding abstract explains serial decoding and parallel draft verification.

B.decision_reason: Cache-off baseline, paired replay, and p50/p95/quality threshold are specified; memory budget remains unset.
B.comments: KVFlow tests a different multi-agent cache-management system; its output-length trend is mechanistically relevant but not a measured Qwen3-8B gain.

cases.question: Entire long paper or iterative selected-passage inspection for paper QA?

claim_scores.claim: On QASPER evidence retrieval, the D3 authors report 99.6% of their best zero-shot baseline performance using 26% of its tokens.
claim_scores.reason: D3 §5.1 reports 99.6% Evidence-F1 performance at 26% token use versus Map-Reduce Optimized; the claim omits that named comparator and that this is evidence retrieval, not answer correctness.

claim_scores.claim: The FinanceBench paper identifies missed relevant pages or chunks despite finding the correct long document.
claim_scores.reason: FinanceBench abstract explicitly identifies correct-document retrieval with missed answer page/chunk.

A.decision_reason: Whole-paper comparator, same-question test, and answer/evidence/token thresholds are specified.
A.comments: D3 is an evidence-retrieval result for a structured summary of the entire paper, not a direct test of iterative selected-passage inspection. The local matched test is essential.

claim_scores.claim: Long-context model performance can degrade when relevant information sits in the middle of a long input.
claim_scores.reason: Lost in the Middle abstract reports degradation for evidence positioned in the middle of long context.

claim_scores.claim: A QASPER document-QA system explicitly separated text extraction, evidence retrieval, and answer generation and reported a 7.19 Answer-F1 gain over its baselines.
claim_scores.reason: DRC abstract reports three stages and +7.19 Answer-F1 over existing baselines; the claim does not identify the particular baseline/comparison.

claim_scores.claim: LongRAG argues that passage chunking can lose global context and noisy retrieval can obscure evidence, motivating some access to broader structure.
claim_scores.reason: LongRAG abstract identifies global-context loss from chunking and noise from poor retrieval.

B.decision_reason: Whole-paper comparator, paired feasible-paper test, and support/token/failure thresholds are specified.
B.comments: Lost-in-the-Middle and DRC support caution about whole-paper input and retrieval, but neither measures this code-execution reader. Feasibility stratum handles context limits.

cases.question: Teacher-generated trajectories or manually corrected failures when 100 more can be reviewed?

claim_scores.claim: ROSS argues historical rollouts contain mistakes and redundant actions that should not all be imitated, and applies supervision selectively.
claim_scores.reason: ROSS abstract says historical rollouts may include mistakes, abandoned attempts, and redundant actions, motivating selected-loss supervision.

claim_scores.claim: Reflective Recovery turns failed prefixes into recovery examples and reports gains on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
claim_scores.reason: Reflective Recovery abstract describes failed prefixes converted to recovery data and math-benchmark gains.

claim_scores.claim: SCoRe found offline supervised correction traces can suffer distribution mismatch and behavior collapse, so corrected traces are not guaranteed to teach recovery.
claim_scores.reason: SCoRe abstract explicitly reports distribution mismatch and behavior collapse for offline correction-trace SFT.

A.decision_reason: Teacher-trace comparator, matched 50/50 review, and example-yield or yield-per-hour threshold are specified.
A.comments: Recovery studies support the concept but do not prove manual corrections beat teacher traces on paper QA. Screening and later held-out SFT test remain necessary.

claim_scores.claim: PROOF-Gen reports that generate-and-filter teacher data discards hard failed scenarios and proposes recovering passing traces from failures.
claim_scores.reason: PROOF-Gen abstract describes generate-and-filter discarding failed hard cases and per-scenario recovery of passing teacher traces.

claim_scores.claim: The SRC study uses bounded teacher review to locate harmful deviations in student agent branches.
claim_scores.reason: SRC abstract describes fixed-horizon teacher branch review to localize first harmful deviation.

B.decision_reason: Teacher-trace comparator, matched 50/50 review, and useful-supervision yield threshold are specified; later training threshold is unset.
B.comments: PROOF-Gen recovers failed teacher scenarios and SRC reviews web-agent branches; neither directly establishes manual student-failure correction superiority here.

review_limitations: This review uses only the anonymized cases file and cited primary paper/document pages; it does not verify local project measurements, human evidence labels, or feasibility of proposed tests.

Several qualitative facts were verified from paper abstracts; numeric and methodological claims were checked in full-text sections where needed. An accurate source claim does not itself prove benefit for this Qwen workload.
